Corroboration

/kuh-ROB-uh-RAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Corroboration means independent supporting evidence that backs up a claim, statement, or theory.

Before the editor would print the whistleblower's account, she demanded corroboration from a second employee inside the plant.

Worked Example

The driver's claim that hail had dented his car roof received corroboration from the weather service's storm log, which recorded golf-ball-sized hail on his street that same afternoon.

The driver only claimed the hail damage, but the weather service's storm log is an independent record confirming that hail really fell on his street that day. That outside evidence backing up his claim is exactly what corroboration is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

confirmation: Confirmation is the everyday word for being assured that something is true — a text confirming plans counts. Corroboration is heavier and more formal: independent evidence, from a separate outside source, backing up a serious claim. Any reassurance can be confirmation; only outside evidence earns the name corroboration.

substantiation: Substantiation is the act of supplying proof for your own claim — the prover's effort to back up what was said, often when it is disputed. Corroboration comes from elsewhere: a separate, independent source that backs the claim up. You substantiate your own story; corroboration arrives from outside it.

verification: Verification is the act of checking a claim or fact against a reliable standard — you verify by looking it up yourself. Corroboration is not a check you run but backing that arrives: a second, independent source confirming the claim. Verification is your own checking; corroboration is outside support.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

contradiction: a statement or fact that directly conflicts with a claim

disproof: evidence showing that a claim is false

Where it sits · how firmly the claim is backed — hint → support → corroboration

hint vs. corroboration: A hint merely nudges you toward believing something, while corroboration independently confirms it.

support vs. corroboration: Support lends weight to a claim, but corroboration comes from a separate outside source that locks the claim down.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — cor-

Prefix — cor-: together, thoroughly (a form of com-)

Root — -robor-

Root — -robor-: to strengthen (Latin robur, 'strength; oak')

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Cor- (thoroughly) plus the Latin root robur (oak-strength) plus -ation literally builds 'a thorough strengthening': corroboration is evidence that strengthens a claim until it stands as solid as oak.

Use the root in a new word: robust

Use the root in a new word: robust: The same Latin root robur, meaning oak-strength, gives us robust, which describes anything sturdy and strong, like a robust bridge design.

Word Choice

formal / legal-academic

Common in courtrooms, science, and research writing. Watch out for the look-alike 'collaboration,' which means working together; corroboration is about independent evidence backing up a claim.
